title: cascade-detection-after-shadow-run-flapping-analysis-and-recovery-checklist
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: During a staged rollout where we routed 10% traffic to model-v2 as shadow and 2% as live canary, we observed intermittent request flapping—a short-lived spike of 502/503-like responses and elevated token-latency for ~3 minutes that correlated with concurrent cache priming. This ticket captures the investigation, the causal hypotheses we validated, and a concrete recovery / prevention checklist for future staged rollouts.

What happened: At 2026-02-27 14:12 UTC a scheduled canary was promoted to receive traffic mirrored from v1. Shadow telemetry showed an early anomaly: a subpopulation of requests experienced a 30–40% increase in per-token latency and transient model inference failures. The hosted fallback system routed affected requests to model-v1 but the automated rollback did not trigger because our confidence heuristic relied primarily on aggregate error rate rather than short-lived, high-severity spikes.

Key findings: 1) KV-cache keyspace skew: model-v2 cache priming caused a temporary eviction thrash on hosts that also served v1 traffic due to shared LRU buckets on a small subset of nodes. 2) Telemetry contract mismatch: the canary alarm was defined at 5-min rolling error-rate; the incident window was ~3 minutes and invisible to that threshold. 3) Rollback confidence scoring gap: our rollback autopilot required sustained signal across multiple metrics; short high-severity bursts weren’t weighted sufficiently. 4) Observability latency: dashboards aggregated by region hid per-host outliers; single-host failure propagated through routing and amplified due to traffic burst routing.

Decisions & action orientation: Instead of incremental alerts only, we propose a dual-path safety approach: (A) fast-path fast-abort that looks at severity-weighted short-window spikes on token-latency and 5xx-like error classes, and (B) slow-path confirmation that uses multi-metric corroboration for longer windows to avoid false positives. We also propose changing cache isolation policies for future canaries (pinning cache namespaces to model variants on mixed-host clusters) and adding a synthetic steady-state test run prior to public split.

Outcome: Implemented a temporary manual mitigation on 2026-03-02 (evacuate mixed-host pods and reduce canary live traffic to 0%), plus the follow-ups below for automation and runbook updates.

Why this is different from prior rollouts: Many prior tickets address rollbacks and canary failures at an outcome level; this incident exposed an observability/decision boundary problem where short, high-severity bursts bypass aggregate alarms and our automation tolerances. The follow-ups emphasize measurement granularity, confidence-weighted abort heuristics, and structural cache isolation to prevent cross-variant impact.
comments: 2026-03-01 Riley Chen: Initial triage — captured logs, flamegraphs, and request traces. Noted eviction spikes on node pool gpu-pool-2b. Parking this as priority; assigning to Aisha for root-cause validation.

2026-03-03 Aisha Khan: Reproduced eviction pattern in stress lab by priming two variants concurrently on a 4-node replica set. Confirmed LRU eviction churn with existing kernel-level allocator and shared cache buckets. Opened PR to add cache-namespace pinning and an integration test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4125
2026-03-04 Miguel Torres: Observability adjustments — added 1-min percentile view and per-host heatmap tile to the rollout dashboard. Early test shows spike visible at 30s granularity.

2026-03-06 Devansh Patel: Reviewed rollback confidence weights and suggested severity scoring: +3 for 5xx bursts, +2 for token-latency P99 > baseline * 2, -1 for single-host-only events. Implemented a provisional evaluator in feature-flagged autopilot branch.
2026-03-08 QA Bot: Synthetic steady-state test executed against model-v2 in staging for 45 minutes; no eviction observed after cache-namespace pinning applied. Attached perf run ID perf-20260308-77.
2026-03-10 Product review (Sofia Martins): Approved checklist and asked to add customer communication draft for affected small set of enterprise users. Assigned to Aisha to prepare message.
2026-03-11 Security (Anya Lebedev): No secrets exposure related to this incident. Confirmed KMS unaffected. Marking security_review_required=false.

2026-03-12 Riley Chen: Current status — PRs merged to staging, autopilot severity weights behind feature flag, dashboards updated. Next: run canary smoke with modified autopilot on non-prod region and runbook update review.
2026-03-12 Aisha Khan: Added follow-up tasks and owners to this ticket. Requesting ops on-call for verification during next smoke run (2026-03-15).
acceptance_criteria: Add a short-window (<=1 minute) severity-weighted abort rule in autopilot and test it in staging behind a feature flag.
Introduce model-specific cache-namespace pinning to prevent cross-variant eviction on mixed clusters and validate via stress test.
Expose per-host 30s heatmap and P99 token-latency on rollout dashboards; provide an audit-friendly snapshot in runbook artifacts.
Update the staged-rollout runbook with the new fast-path abort checklist and a customer-communication template for brief incidents.
Execute two non-prod canaries with the full changes and confirm no transient 5xx or token-latency spikes in 95% of runs.
Postmortem summary merged to confluence with timeline, RCA, and lessons learned, plus links to PRs and perf runs.
